title: Five variants of your Rerun pick: the arm on the left, your tabs on the right
kicker: /babble 5 · the Trajectory Tracking Agent's run p6s on workspace-dev-029 (target vs solution) · UR5e URDF · real Rerun 0.40
brief: Your Nov 24 note: "I wanted 5 new variants of my pick not the 5 old looks". Your pick is R3 (the 3D arm on the left half) with your tabs on the right (q · qd · qdd · qddd · q/qd/qdd · TCP). Every variant keeps that frame and changes what's inside it: what the 3D side shows, how the tabs are organised, how the plots are drawn, how you find moments, and how a tracking run (target vs solution) appears. V1 is what's built (robot_msgs main) and stays the default until you pick. Each one is a single function, a JointTrajectory + the URDF (+ an optional target) in, an .rrd out. All five are filmed in the real viewer on the same run.
defaultWhy: V2 · Target vs run scores 91/100. It's V1 plus the one thing V1 can't do: show a tracking run. The arm stays plain steel, and the run's deviation from its target is drawn ×50 as a thin magenta skeleton with an arrow labelled with the true offset. An Error tab opens first, with the agent's own ruler (RMS 1.09 mm, worst 2.11 mm at 1.42 s), each joint's error in degrees, and a target-vs-run table at the playhead. Your six tabs follow, each with the target as a pale line under the run. With no target (a plan) it's V1, unchanged. Next best: V4 · By joint + events (79), whose clickable Events log is the part worth splicing in.
decisionHinge: Whether this viewer is mostly for tracking runs or for plans. V2's lead comes from target vs solution (20 % of the score). With no target, V2 and V1 look the same. If finding moments matters more than seeing the error, V4 closes in: its Events tab lists start, via points, peak speed, closest to a limit and worst error, and clicking a row seeks there. The likely splice is V2 + V4's Events log as one more tab, + V3's limit tint as a toggle.
invariants: Your frame in every variant: the URDF arm in 3D on the left half, always; tabs on the right half; angles in degrees.

The same run: the Trajectory Tracking Agent's saved run p6s (best of generation 0) on the UR5e tour workspace-dev-029 (3.2 s): its target, its solution from the joint encoders, and the agent's own tool-error ruler. Both tool points come from the URDF's forward kinematics.
One function per variant: save(path, traj, *, robot, tool=None, target=None, target_tool=None, extras=None). robot_msgs is not edited (today's robot= call is unchanged).

Every frame is from the real Rerun 0.40 web viewer, loaded once, with the playhead set through the viewer's own handle. Each variant was re-filmed by an independent checker, its defects fixed, and re-checked.
boundary: Prototypes in traj_compare/docs/proposals/rerun-pick-variants-2026-11-24/v1…v5 (make.py + two .rrd each; they open in the native viewer too). Nothing is in robot_msgs beyond V1, which is main. Label placement in V2, V4 and V5 is fitted to the opening camera at 1600×1000, so orbiting can move labels onto things.

variants.name: Target vs run

variants.name: Limit-lit
variants.thesis: The arm itself tells you how hard each joint is working: every link is tinted live by its joint's worst % of limit (green, amber ≥ 80 %, red ≥ 95 %). A '% of limit' tab leads, and the recording opens on the moment closest to a limit.
variants.bestWhen: Checking whether a trajectory or a controller pushes the robot to its limits, and where.
variants.losesWhen: A time-optimal plan rides its limits most of the time, so the arm is mostly red and the colour stops discriminating. The tracking error isn't shown.

decisions.label: Tint
decisions.value: Each link re-coloured over time by its joint's max of |q| to its limit, |qd|/vmax and |qdd|/amax; a legend under the arm gives each joint's number.

decisions.label: Opens at the moment
decisions.value: Rerun has no start-time setting, so the file writes the rows from the moment onward first; it opened at 0.40 s on 7 of 7 loads (web viewer).
